s1.syndrome_frame: Acute decompensation of chronic liver disease with hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, and recurrent pleural effusion
salient_findings: Elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT > 1000 U/L)
Positive HCV antibody with high viral load
key_facts: 61-year-old woman with cirrhosis secondary to alcohol use disorder
History of esophageal varices, rectal varices, ascites, and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
Remote history of intranasal cocaine use and multiple tattoos
No history of blood transfusions before 1990, intravenous drug use, or high-risk sexual behavior
Developed clinical decompensation requiring multiple paracenteses, thoracenteses, and blood transfusions
Had a dental extraction three months prior to presentation
Mental status showed acute decline
Progressive deterioration led to increased encephalopathy with concurrent hypotension
Elevated AST and ALT (> 1000 U/L)
Negative urine drug screen
Negative blood cultures
Initial negative HCV antibody, later positive
HCV viral load: 4,510,319 copies/mL
Liver explant histology showed micronodular cirrhosis with dense fibrosis
